bull.t: Strong revenue growth and healthy operating margins
bull.b: Sustained top-line growth with high gross and solid EBIT/EBITDA margins reflects a scalable licensing model and efficient content delivery. Durable margins show the business can convert incremental revenue into operating profit, supporting reinvestment in content and platform capabilities over time.

bull.t: Improving cash generation and positive free cash flow
bull.b: Rebounding operating cash flow and positive free cash flow indicate improving internal funding capacity. Recurring subscription revenue and better FCF reduce reliance on external financing, enabling gradual deleveraging, capex funding, and discretionary investment in product and content over the medium term.

bull.t: Editorial strength and AI/custom content momentum
bull.b: Growing editorial demand and rapid expansion in custom/AI-enabled offerings show strategic differentiation. Unique archive, event coverage, and high-value custom video/AI work drive higher yields and stickier enterprise relationships, strengthening long-term pricing power and product differentiation.

bear.t: High leverage and significant interest burden
bear.b: Very high leverage and sizable interest expense materially constrain financial flexibility. Heavy debt servicing reduces free cash available for content investment or strategic M&A and raises refinancing risk if revenue or margins falter, making capital structure a persistent overhang.

bear.t: Net losses and inconsistent bottom-line profitability
bear.b: Despite strong gross and operating margins, net losses and negative ROE reflect interest, litigation reserves and episodic charges. Inconsistent net profitability undermines retained earnings, limits shareholder return capacity, and increases dependence on cash generation to stabilize equity value.

bear.t: Merger termination, litigation payouts and balance-sheet strain
bear.b: Termination of the Shutterstock deal removes a potential scale and cost-savings pathway while forcing secured-note redemptions and creating near-term liquidity demands. Coupled with litigation payouts, these structural events raise refinancing and financing-cost risk and constrain strategic optionality.
